body.statement: For every \((p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathfrak T\), every \(P\in\mathcal M_{p,k}(m,M,s,V)\), and every \(|S|\le2k\), the sharp information-specific lower endpoint is \[B(S)=(\mu_1-\mu_0)^2+(c_{1,S}-c_{0,S})^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{SS}^{-1}(c_{1,S}-c_{0,S})+(\sqrt{r_1(S)}-\sqrt{r_0(S)})^2.\] It is attained by coupling the two conditional Gaussian residuals through one common standard normal.
body.justification: This proposition makes the causal partial-identification endpoint explicit and supplies the algebraic object whose information increments can be compared.
body.gap: Lin et al. (2025), Example 3.8 and Lemma 5.1, give Gaussian conditional-transport formulas in special models; the present formula covers arbitrary retained coordinate sets and records direct information-specific attainment.
body.consumer: A trial planner can evaluate the sharp lower bound on mean squared individual effects from arm-specific first and second moments for any candidate baseline panel.
